title: What to watch at the open
text: Stock futures, which are bets on where prices will open, were a little lower early Tuesday after Monday's tech selloff. The big event is tonight: NVIDIA reports its results after the market closes. On Monday the five AI supplier stocks on our list fell about 5.3% on average, and the four big AI platform companies fell about 2.7%. Expect a nervous, choppy day until NVIDIA's numbers are out. Prices on this page are Monday's closing prices.

title: NVIDIA reports tonight, its first report since the CEO change
text: NVIDIA closed Monday at $156.14, only about 5% above its lowest price of the past year ($148.80). This is its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO last week, with Colette Kress leading for now. A report can push a stock up or down a lot in one day. Because NVIDIA is so big, its move can also pull chip suppliers like AMD, TSMC, Broadcom and Vertiv, and funds like QQQ, along with it.

title: Alphabet waits near its one year low as Anthropic prices its stock
text: Alphabet ended Monday at $283.72, about 4% above its one year low of $272.11. Anthropic, an AI company that Alphabet and Amazon own pieces of, is expected to set its final share price on Wednesday and start trading Thursday. Reports say buyers asked for about six times more shares than are for sale. How that debut goes may move Alphabet and Amazon.

title: Calm stocks are holding near their highs
text: While chip stocks are far below their peaks (Vertiv is about 50% under its one year high), the dividend fund SCHD is only 1.4% below its high and Eli Lilly is 2.8% below. Slower, steadier companies often hold up better when fast growing stocks get hit. That is one reason people mix both kinds.

title: Lesson 54: What are stock futures?
text: The stock market opens at 9:30 am New York time, but people want to trade on news that comes out overnight. Stock futures let them do that. A future is a deal to buy or sell an index, like the S&P 500, at a set price on a later date, and futures trade almost all day and night. So when the news says 'futures are down 0.5%', it means traders expect stocks to open a bit lower. It is a weather forecast, not a promise: the real market can turn around once it opens. Long term investors usually do not need to act on futures; they are just a clue about the mood of the morning.

title: Where today's numbers come from
text: Prices, daily changes, beta, 52 week ranges and sector moves come from FMP and show Monday's close. Analyst targets and company ratios come from FMP for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE. For TSMC we kept last reading's one year low ($266.82) because today's feed showed a much lower number that looks like a data error. The 10 year Treasury yield is a monthly average from Alpha Vantage. News comes from web searches of news sites. Nothing here is advice to buy or sell.
